extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, poets, rhetoricians, literary students, and writers seeking classical guidance on composition and critique
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria from Aristotle's Poetics, Demetrius On Style, and Longinus On the Sublime for composing and judging tragedy, epic, rhetoric, and elevated prose/poetry. Covers plot, character, diction, figures, the sublime, and practical stylistic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimesis (Imitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry and drama are imitations of action and life; their purpose is to represent human actions rather than merely to narrate events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should faithfully represent plausible human actions and motivations; excellence lies in selective, artful imitation that reveals universals through particular incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Plot (Whole with Beginning, Middle, End)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tragedy must be a whole — with a definite beginning, middle, and end — where incidents follow one another by necessity or probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange episodes so each causes the next; avoid loose episodic structure. The whole should be of a certain magnitude sufficient to produce catharsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude (Appropriate Length and Scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plot must be of a suitable size — neither too short to be insignificant nor too long to exceed the audience's comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scope that allows a single unified action to unfold with the right emotional impact; 'magnitude' is judged by the ability to evoke pity and fear appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability / Necessity (Causal Coherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events in the plot should arise from what is probable or necessary within the story's internal logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid improbable contrivances; even surprising turns must be credible in hindsight or follow from character and circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex Plot Elements: Reversal (Peripeteia) and Recognition (Anagnorisis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complex plot includes a reversal of fortune and/or a recognition that together produce heightened tragic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peripeteia and anagnorisis to create sudden but believable changes in the protagonist's circumstances that move the audience emotionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catharsis (Arousal and Purging of Pity and Fear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tragedy aims to arouse pity and fear and thereby to achieve a catharsis — a purgation or clarification of those emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design scenes and character trajectories to elicit compassion and dread, then resolve them to produce emotional release and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character (Ethos) — Consistency and Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should be consistent, believable, and appropriate to their roles; the protagonist is neither wholly good nor wholly bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters' actions must spring from their established dispositions; tragic downfall should result from error or frailty (hamartia) rather than sheer vice or inexplicable malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic Hero Criteria (Middle Rank, Hamartia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tragic hero is typically of noble or elevated status but not perfect; a misstep or error of judgment brings catastrophe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid portraying the hero as irredeemably evil or flawless — sympathy depends on fallibility and proportionality of suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction (Lexis) — Choice and Quality of Language
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of words, metaphors, and phrasing should be appropriate, clear, and effective for the emotions and ideas being expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use apt metaphors and the right level of diction for characters and situation; avoid awkward or mixed metaphors and aim for precision and grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought (Dianoia) — Argument and Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideas, reasoning, and thematic content expressed through speeches and action should be coherent and suited to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speeches should reveal character and advance the plot or theme; thought should be persuasive and organically integrated into the drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody/Chorus (Melos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical elements (chorus, song) are an integral part of tragedy and should enhance the whole, not distract from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate choral song and rhythm where they support mood and meaning; ensure musical parts are integrated with the plot and diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectacle (Opsis) — Visual Effects as Secondary
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectacle (scenery, stage-effects) produces strong sensory impact but is the least artistic element compared to plot and character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely principally on the poet's craft of plot and character; use visual spectacle sparingly and only where it reinforces the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Action over Unity of Time/Place
rubrics_metrics.description: What matters most is unity of action; strict unity of time and place is secondary and only insofar as it serves the plot's unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit temporal and spatial flexibility when necessary for a coherent, unified action — avoid arbitrary deviations that fragment the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic vs Tragedy Distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Epic allows greater magnitude, uses narration rather than continuous dramatic action, and can include multiple plots; tragedy is concentrated, enacted, and unified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose form based on scope and method of representation: epic suits long, multiple actions and digression; tragedy suits tight, enacted unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability in Character Speech (Appropriateness of Diction to Character)
rubrics_metrics.description: What characters say must be suitable to their social rank, temperament, and situation; speech reveals and should match character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid improbable nobility of speech in base characters or undue vulgarity in noble characters unless used deliberately for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Correctness (Demetrius) — Purity of Expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Style must be correct, clear, and free from solecisms; purity and propriety of words are foundational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe grammatical correctness and idiomatic usage; correct minor errors in diction and syntax to preserve clarity and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of Style (Demetrius) — Decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: Style and ornament must be appropriate to subject matter, audience, and occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match plainness or ornament to the seriousness or levity of the subject; avoid mismatches that jar the reader or listener.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornament and Figures (Demetrius) — Use with Restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetorical figures and ornament (metaphor, antithesis, rhythm) enhance style when used tastefully and with measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ figures to illuminate and elevate thought; avoid overwrought ornament that obscures sense or appears affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and Rhythm (Demetrius & Longinus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective style balances variety of expression, cadence, and rhythmic flow to engage and move the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate sentence lengths, employ cadences and pauses, and ensure euphony; monotony undermines effect while controlled variety sustains interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandeur of Thought (Longinus) — Elevation of Conception
rubrics_metrics.description: The sublime arises from great and elevated thought — noble ideas, lofty views, and majestic conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate amplified, expansive thinking and present universal or exalted themes so as to lift the reader's mind beyond the ordinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Emotion and Passion (Longinus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intense feeling and transported passion contribute to sublimity and power in language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow genuine passion to infuse expression; manufactured emotion or mere ornament cannot substitute for real feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noble Diction and Elevated Figures (Longinus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of noble, fitting words and elevated figures of speech (apt metaphors, analogies) are crucial to producing the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer bold, apposite metaphors and dignified phraseology; the right metaphor can illuminate and amplify an idea instantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Construction / Dignified Arrangement (Longinus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositional order, proportion, and arrangement of parts must be dignified and contribute to grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure arguments and episodes so their cumulative effect builds toward sublimity; avoid trivial or disjointed insertions that break elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Bathos and Bombast (Longinus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sublimity must not descend into mere rant, cliché, or tawdry ornament; restraint and context matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against exaggerated, inappropriate language that produces amusement rather than elevation; sublimity requires rightness of tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning from Models and Imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Study and imitate great writers to acquire style, figures, and the means of producing elevated effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitation combined with critical judgment trains the writer: absorb models' strengths but avoid slavish copying and anachronistic clichés.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and Precision (Style Anti-Pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive wordiness or unnecessary ornament weakens impact; precision of expression strengthens persuasive and emotional force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune redundant phrases, avoid pointless amplification, and prefer the most expressive, economical phrasing that preserves dignity and clarity.
